main_text.p: terrorem maximum eam conjecit, & ob hyemem ingruentem iftinc abiens, rurfumque in agrum Laconicum rever-fus, oppidis etiam minoribus occupa-tis univerfum eum miferrime affixit. Deinde in Macedoniam revocatus, rebus illic conftitutis, in Ætolos conver-fus, iftuc neceffitatis eos redegit, ut tum ipfi, tum ipforum focii Lacedæmonii malis fracti talibus conditionibus pacem petere & admittere cogerentur, quales ab hoftibus dabantur. Factum, cum bellum duraffet annos quafi tres, & paulo ante in Italia male contra Annibalem Pænorum ducem pugnatum effet à Romanis ad Trafimenum Hetruriæ lacum. Res gefta hoc bello nomine Lacedæmoniorum aufpiciis regis Lycurgi. Belli hujus jam ardentis initio, cum in Triphylia regione Eseis & Meffeniis & Arcadibus finitima feliciter rem gereret Philippus, regno pariter & vitæ Lycurgi infidiæ domi ftructæ à Chilone quodam itemmatis regii viro, qui ob genus fe regno digniorem censebat, & fibi ab ephoris, à quibus præteritus, & regnum Lycurgo venditum erat, infignem iniuriam esse factam arbitrabatur. Confilii autem ejus erat, exemplo Cleomenis novæ fortitionis & [illegible, ~3 letters]partitionis agri spem plebi subjicere: quà
[illegible marginal marks at the foot of the left margin, ~2 letters each]

page.notes: The left-margin marks at the foot of the page (around the lines "partitionis" and "quà" and below) are small and partly overlapping; they are read only as approximate letter groups and marked illegible. "Eseis" for the place name is uncertain: the printed form reads as "Efeis" with long s, and the classical name may be Elis, so it is copied as the printed letters with long s rendered as s. "subjicere" keeps the printed j as consonant. The word "affixit" is read from the scan and may be a printed "afflixit" with long s. Printed hyphenated line-end words are kept with their hyphens.
